official.deadline_note: DAAD sets the deadline by country of origin, so there is no single central date. Verified on DAAD's own listing for the current cycle: Jordan 31.08.2026 (selection February 2027, start of funding October 2027); Costa Rica, Colombia, Mexico and other Latin American countries 03.09.2026 (funding decision March 2027, start winter semester 2027); Kenya 30.09.2026 (selection presumably February 2027, start October 2027); Vietnam and the Indonesia/Malaysia/Timor-Leste region 21.10.2026 (selection approx. February 2027, start October 2027). The portal closes at 24.00 hrs (CET or CEST) on the country deadline.
official.application_cycle: Winter term 2027/28 intake; applications possible between 1 June 2026 and the country-specific deadline
official.status_note: The DAAD listing states 'Currently you cannot apply for this programme.' The window for the winter term 27/28 intake ran from 1 June 2026 to each country's own deadline (31 August - 21 October 2026), and all eligible countries' dates have now passed. Funding decisions are taken around February-March 2027 and funding usually begins on 1 October 2027. DAAD states that application deadlines are updated annually in the second quarter.
official.tuition_coverage_note: "It must be a tuition-free Master's degree programme." and "Please note that the DAAD does not cover tuition fees" - the chosen programme itself must charge no tuition.
benefits: Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover

On application after start of funding: monthly rent subsidy, monthly allowance for accompanying members of family, subsidy for justified additional costs in case of disability or chronic illness, reimbursement of carbon offset payments for air travel

Language benefits on application (funding period over six months): payment of online language course fees, a German language course in Germany before the programme starts if necessary, allowance for a personally chosen German language course, reimbursement of the TestDaF or DSH test fee
eligibility: High-achieving students from developing and emerging countries, applying from one of the 24 listed countries of origin (Belize, Cambodia, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Ghana, Guatemala, Honduras, Indonesia, Jordan, Kenya, Laos, Malaysia, Mexico, Myanmar, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Venezuela, Vietnam)
First degree recognised in Germany (e.g. a Bachelor's degree) completed by the application deadline at the latest; applicants who already hold a Master's degree by the deadline cannot apply
As a rule the most recent university degree should not date back more than 6 years at the time of the application deadline
The application cannot be considered if the applicant has been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline
Above-average academic performance; the legal and subject-specific admission requirements for a Master's degree in Germany must be fulfilled (Master's programmes are generally consecutive)
Proof of at least level B1 in the language of instruction of the chosen study programme
requirements: Funding covers a complete Master's degree (full-time, on-campus) at a state or state-recognised university in Germany in mathematics, computer science, natural sciences or engineering
Study programmes with integrated stays outside Germany are excluded
Interdisciplinary degree programmes must have a designated STEM focus
It must be a tuition-free Master's degree programme; the DAAD formally excludes programmes that charge tuition fees
Funding is not possible for a Master's programme that has already begun in Germany; funding is only available for degree programmes starting in winter term 27/28
Applicants must state the entire desired scholarship period (10 to 24 months) in the application and are themselves responsible for submitting their university admission application on time
documents: Full curriculum vitae in tabular form (max. 3 pages) and letter of motivation (1-3 pages) on the academic and personal reasons for the study project
Letter of admission to the study programme at the host university in Germany (if not yet received, it must be submitted before the funding period begins)
DAAD form 'Information about your preferred master programmes', duly completed (up to 5 Master's programmes)
Current overview of grades/transcript of records with individual grades and all university degree certificates already obtained (or a preliminary document if not yet awarded)
Certificate of the language(s) of instruction of the chosen programme, no older than 3 years, at least level B1

One recent supporting letter of recommendation on a DAAD form from a university teacher, plus the passport/national identity card data page (for refugees: Refugee ID card and UNHCR registration/official proof of asylum)
selection_criteria: Academic qualification: academic achievements, course of studies, knowledge of the language(s) of instruction or working language(s), and if applicable relevant internships and work experience
Quality of the study project and of the preparation (preliminary information, choice of degree programme, host university, establishment of contacts) and its integration into the academic career path

Potential of the applicant: motivation (academic and personal reasons, German language skills if different from the working language), prospects of the stay for further development, extracurricular commitment
Aspects of equal opportunities, e.g. disability, chronic or prolonged illness, raising children, caring for relatives, refugee background, extensive employment required to finance studies

Only complete applications with all mandatory documents are considered; pre-selection is based on the submitted documents, and pre-selected applicants are invited to an interview (on site or virtual) with an independent selection committee of university teachers
coverage: Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover
Tuition fees are not covered - the funded Master's programme must be tuition-free
application_method: Applications are made online through the DAAD portal, possible between 1 June and the stated country application deadline
Register in the DAAD portal and complete the online application in full
Generate the letter of recommendation form in the portal ('Create Letter of Recommendation Form'), send it to a university teacher, and upload the completed form
Upload all documents as PDF files in the 'Attachments' section and submit the application online; the portal closes at 24.00 hrs (CET or CEST) on the last application day
official.application_route: Apply online through the DAAD portal: register, generate and circulate the DAAD recommendation form, complete the online form, upload all mandatory PDF attachments, and submit before your country's deadline.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must live in and apply from one of the 24 listed countries of origin; an application cannot be considered if the applicant has been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is aimed at applicants from the 24 listed developing and emerging countries; applicants from other countries are asked to contact the DAAD to find out whether they are eligible.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: STEM subjects only: mathematics, computer science, natural sciences and engineering, with interdisciplinary programmes requiring a designated STEM focus. Funded by the German Federal Foreign Office.
official.duration: 10 months to a maximum of 24 months, depending on the standard period of study of the chosen full-time Master's degree programme; after the first year academic achievements are assessed and the scholarship continues if successful completion within a reasonable period is expected.
official.description: The DAAD supports the qualification and employability of young academics and future professionals from developing and emerging countries, offering them the opportunity to continue their academic and professional career in innovation-driving STEM fields in Germany with a Master's degree in mathematics, computer science, natural sciences and engineering.
official.region: Study in Germany; applicants from the 24 listed developing and emerging countries of origin
official.program_type: Master's degree scholarship (full-time, on-campus, tuition-free programme)
official.english_requirement: Proof of current proficiency in the language of instruction of the chosen programme (German, English, or German and English) at at least level B1; for English-taught programmes DAAD lists e.g. Cambridge English, Cambridge Business, IELTS, ISE, TOEFL iBT, TOEFL Essentials, TOEIC, PTE Academic, onSET English and Duolingo English Test. Specific certificates and higher levels may be required by the host university's admission rules, and those test fees are not reimbursed by the DAAD.

verification.notes: Award value (EUR 992 per month, EUR 460 annual study allowance, insurance, travel allowance), eligibility rules, documents and selection criteria were read from the DAAD scholarship database listing for this programme (print version updated 2026-10-11); country deadlines were verified on DAAD's own country-filtered listing and on the DAAD Regional Office Indonesia page.

applicant_utility.summary: This DAAD scheme funds a full, tuition-free STEM Master's in Germany for graduates from 24 listed developing and emerging countries, paying EUR 992 per month plus insurance contributions, a travel allowance on application and an annual study allowance of EUR 460 for 10 to 24 months starting 1 October 2027. The winter 2027/28 round closed on country-specific dates between 31 August and 21 October 2026 - Jordan earliest, Vietnam and the Indonesia/Malaysia/Timor-Leste region latest - so the realistic next chance is the call DAAD is expected to open around June 2027. It is a living-costs stipend rather than a full ride: tuition is explicitly not covered, which is why the chosen programme must charge no fees at all. Treat your own country's deadline as the binding one, because the dates are not synchronised across eligible countries.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Above-average STEM graduates from the 24 eligible countries whose first degree is less than about six years old, who can win a place on a tuition-free German Master's and need support with living costs rather than tuition.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country of origin appears on the programme's list of 24 eligible countries and find its own deadline, since the dates differ by country.
Brief your recommender early: the DAAD recommendation form can only be generated inside the portal while the application window is open.
Book your language test roughly three months ahead - DAAD needs B1 in the language of instruction and many universities demand more for admission.
Shortlist up to five tuition-free Master's programmes and complete DAAD's 'Information about your preferred master programmes' form; fee-charging programmes are formally excluded.
Track each host university's own admission deadline separately, because your admission has to be secured before funding can begin.
Arrange certified German or English translations of transcripts and certificates before the window opens, as translations must be uploaded alongside the originals.
common_rejection_risks: An incomplete file: DAAD excludes applications missing any mandatory document for formal reasons before anyone reads them.
Applying for a Master's that charges tuition fees, which the DAAD formally excludes.
Already holding a Master's degree by the deadline, or having lived in Germany for more than 15 months - both are hard disqualifiers.
A first degree older than the six-year guideline at the application deadline.
A generic motivation letter: the interview exists partly to test authenticity, and motivation carries explicit weight in the criteria.
Missing the host university's own admission deadline and therefore starting the scholarship without a study place.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees are not covered (the programme must be tuition-free). You still fund qualified translations, language-test fees (DAAD reimburses only a TestDaF or DSH fee, and only after you hold the Letter of Award), any fees your host university itself charges for application or enrolment, and any shortfall between the EUR 992 monthly payment and real rent in expensive cities - the rent subsidy and the family allowance are granted only on application.
document_audit: The language certificate must be no older than three years and must be uploaded even if your chosen university requires no language proof.
The recommendation letter has to be on the DAAD form generated in the portal - a generic reference from your professor will not do.
Only PDF files can be uploaded, and anything not issued in German or English needs its translation uploaded together with it.
If your degree certificate has not been issued yet, upload a preliminary document and make sure the final certificate arrives before the scholarship starts.
Watch the format limits: CV max. 3 pages, motivation letter 1-3 pages.
Upload the passport data page (or Refugee ID card plus UNHCR registration) under 'Miscellaneous', not among the academic documents.
alerts: Deadlines are set per country of origin and are not synchronised: the last cycle ran from 31 August 2026 (Jordan) to 21 October 2026 (Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Timor-Leste), so plan against the earliest plausible date.

The winter term 2027/28 window has now closed for every eligible country; DAAD says deadlines are updated annually in the second quarter, so expect a fresh call around June 2027 rather than trusting recycled dates from aggregators.
The portal shuts at 24:00 CET/CEST on the deadline day and DAAD explicitly advises not to submit on the final day in case of technical problems.
Funding only starts for winter-term programmes that have not already begun in Germany, normally on 1 October (earlier only if you take a German language course beforehand).
Selection happens around February-March 2027 and includes an interview with an independent committee of university teachers, on site or online.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the DAAD portal, generate and send the recommendation form to your referee, complete the online form, upload every mandatory PDF, and submit before your country's deadline; document pre-selection is followed by an interview with the independent selection committee.
